name: std::copy_backward

declarations.code:
template <class BidirIt1, class BidirIt2>

BidirIt2 copy_backward(BidirIt1 first, BidirIt1 last, BidirIt2 d_last);

intro:
Copies the elements from the range [first, last) to another range ending at d_last. The elements are copied in reverse order (the last element is copied first), but their relative order is preserved.

The behavior is undefined if d_last is within (first, last]. std::copy must be used instead of std::copy_backward in that case.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
first, last

 -

 the range of the elements to copy from


 d_last

 -

 the end of the destination range


 Type requirements


 -BidirIt must meet the requirements of LegacyBidirectionalIterator.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: Iterator to the last element copied.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: When copying overlapping ranges, std::copy is appropriate when copying to the left (beginning of the destination range is outside the source range) while std::copy_backward is appropriate when copying to the right (end of the destination range is outside the source range).
